title: Federal Rule 14 — third-party practice
summary: Impleader brings a nonparty into an action because that person may owe the defending party all or part of the liability asserted by the plaintiff. Common examples involve indemnity or contribution.

sections.Role in the course: Impleader brings a nonparty into an action because that person may owe the defending party all or part of the liability asserted by the plaintiff. Common examples involve indemnity or contribution.
sections.What to examine: Identify the original claim and the substantive source of the proposed third party’s liability to the defendant. Show why that liability depends on or passes through the original claim. Then examine Rule 14’s procedure and the separate jurisdictional requirements.
